name: Spline + Website
philosophy: A designer-made micro 3D moment adds delight to a clear product page. The scene decorates and demonstrates; the page does the explaining.
principles: One small scene with one purpose
Page and scene talk to each other through events
The scene is edited visually, by a designer
The page works fully without it
visualIdentity: Friendly, tactile SaaS: soft shapes, gentle materials, a playful object matched to a crisp interface.
artDirection: Match the scene's colours and material to the design system. Keep the object toy-like and simple.

layout.composition: A product page with a hero or feature visual slot holding the scene. Feature blocks may vary in size; a bento grid is on-style here when items differ.

typography: Friendly modern sans at clear sizes, with tight headlines and short sentences.
colour: Bright, friendly accents from the scene carried into interface details.
contentPresentation: Clear product marketing: what it does, how it works, proof, pricing or next step.
assets: The operator's own Spline scene and a poster of it. The team has never shipped real Spline, so this stays experimental.
animation: Scene reacts to hover and clicks; interface buttons trigger scene events. Micro-interactions throughout.
scrolling: Native scroll. The scene may react to scroll position through events.
responsive: Poster on mobile unless the scene is verified light enough.
avoidFor: Projects without a Spline account or scene

fromTeam: Workbook: Spline never used; Sketchfab GLB and procedural Three.js substituted
Skill: SplineScene behind a poster with events
interpreted: Almost all design guidance: no team evidence yet
